body_markdown:
## Dow Falls 1,833 Points on Midterm Data Center Fears


The[Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/dow-jones-industrial-average-djia-explained/) dropped 1,833.06 points, or 3.44%, to 51,523.06, erasing Wednesday's gain of more than 1,500 points, and the S&P 500 lost 4.36% to 7,353.73, according to CNBC. All three major averages posted their worst day since April 2025, CNBC reported, and CNN said all 11 S&P 500 sectors closed lower.


Investors weighed the political shift after Democrats won both chambers of Congress. Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, a Democrat, campaigned on a temporary data center moratorium and an end to certain tax incentives for data center builders, CNN reported, noting that Texas is a major hub for Google, Meta, Oracle and OpenAI data centers. CNBC reported that Sen. Bernie Sanders, who caucuses with Democrats, called for a national data center moratorium.


> "We want a slowdown in the AI buildout. It was too frenzied and speculative," Ed Yardeni, president of Yardeni Research, told CNN.


Investors moved toward safer assets as the selloff deepened. The Cboe Volatility Index, or VIX, rose roughly 70% for its biggest one-day jump in almost two years, and the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.84%, its lowest in two months, according to CNN.


## Stock Futures Slip Before the October Jobs Report


Stock index futures extended the decline in Thursday evening trading. Shortly after 6 p.m. ET, S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq-100 futures were each down 0.4%, and Dow futures had lost 201 points, or 0.4%, according to[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/05/stock-market-today-live-updates.html) .


The selling reached Asia on Friday. Japan's Nikkei slumped 6%, South Korea's KOSPI fell more than 8% to trigger a circuit breaker, and Taiwan's market dropped more than 8%, Reuters reported. CNBC said the Nikkei 225 entered[bear market territory](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/bull-market-vs-bear-market-definition-examples-and-how-it-compares/) , more than 20% below its June peak.


Traders now turn to the October employment report. CNBC reported the Dow Jones consensus for the release against September's figures:


Indicator September (reported) October (Dow Jones consensus)


Nonfarm payrolls +29,000 +59,000


Unemployment rate 4.2% 4.2%


## When Is the October Jobs Report?


The October Employment Situation report is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. ET on Friday, Nov. 6, according to the[Bureau of Labor Statistics release schedule](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/empsit.htm) . The November report follows on Dec. 4.


## What Does the October Jobs Report Mean for the Fed?


Markets priced about a 70% chance of a quarter-point rate hike at the Federal Reserve's Dec. 9 meeting, according to the CME FedWatch Tool as cited by CNBC. CNBC reported that those odds had stood at 82.7% on Wednesday, and that the Fed's current target range is 3.75% to 4.00%.
